text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has decided to hold national and provincial assemblies elections on the same day, February 3.

- The caretaker government had rejected Pakistan People's Party and Pakistan Muslim League objections over plans to conclude new agreements with the World Bank and the IMF and said it had a mandate to stem the economic rot of the country.
- Ghinwa Bhutto, widow of Mir Murtaza Bhutto, has formally taken over as head of the Pakistan People's Party (Shaheed Bhutto group), to replace her husband.
- Workers of the religious Sunni Tehrik group held demonstrations and set tyres on fire against the induction of a Qadiani, regarded as a non-Muslim, as minister in the Sindh cabinet.
- Deputy Chairman Planning Commisson Hafiz Pasha has said the government was making efforts to turn around the economy by laying the basis for sustained future growth.
- The caretaker government has decided not to privatise the tax collection system, Shahid Javed Burki, Adviser to Prime Minister on Finance and Economic Affairs said.

- The government is considering imposing a farm tax at the rate of 200 rupees ($4.97) per acre and reducting general sales tax slabs from four to two, to comply with the agreed framework of reforms with the IMF.
- A new petroleum policy would be announced this month, Federal Minister for Petroleum and Natural Resources Javed Jabbar said.
- Government officials have accused the previous government of misusing privatisation revencues.
- Pakistan and China will sign an agreement for the promotion of mutual trade and economic cooperation between the two countries.
- The central executive committee of the Pakistan People's Party has elected Nusrat Bhutto, mother of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto, as the chairperson of the party to replace her daughter.
